note: Generator-agnostic prompts for missing brand visuals across LinkedIn, GitHub, the portfolio, and the Notion redirect pages. Project images are intentionally not in this list — they already exist in src/assets/img/projects/. Each slot now exposes 4 variants (v1 = original direction, v2/v3/v4 = alternate directions). Pick the variant that fits the surface, paste `full_prompt` into Nano Banana / Imagen / Midjourney / DALL-E, and save outputs to src/assets/img/branding/<id>__<variant_id>.png so they're served at https://ironmanyg.github.io/hussain-portfolio/assets/img/branding/<id>__<variant_id>.png. The selected final per slot can be aliased to <id>.png for the canonical filename used by the site/LinkedIn/GitHub/Notion.

prompt_principles.summary: Synthesised from Google Cloud's Nano Banana guide, the official Gemini Image API docs, Leonardo's prompt guide, and LetsEnhance's 2026 image-prompt guide.
rules: Write a narrative scene description, not a keyword list. Nano Banana / Imagen / Midjourney v7 all parse natural-language scene direction more reliably than tag soup.
Anchor every prompt with: subject + medium + style + lighting + framing + mood + palette. Drop any axis you don't care about, but never skip lighting — that's the #1 reason images look generic.

For literal in-image text, wrap the exact string in double quotes and keep it short. Define hierarchy explicitly (large headline / smaller subhead / tiny caption) instead of expecting the model to guess.

Use photographic vocabulary to control the camera: focal length (50mm, 85mm, 35mm), angle (low-angle, eye-level, isometric, top-down), lens behaviour (shallow depth of field, bokeh, macro), light setup (three-point softbox, golden hour, hard rim light, ambient overcast).
Use positive framing instead of negative — 'empty desk' beats 'no clutter'. Reserve the negative_prompt field for true exclusions (no faces, no text, no logos).
Specify aspect ratio explicitly even if the generator infers it (e.g., '4:1 horizontal banner', '1.91:1 social card').
When iterating, change ONE variable per round (palette OR composition OR lighting). Shotgun changes make it impossible to learn what helped.

For brand imagery, name the style influence (e.g., 'Pentagram editorial', 'Swiss/International Typographic Style', 'Dieter Rams product minimalism') — one director name carries more signal than five adjectives.
prompt_principles.negative_prompt_baseline_for_brand_asset: no AI-blurred backgrounds, no stock-photo skylines, no glowing circuits, no binary code rain, no neon, no decorative emoji, no faces, no people, no Anthropic/Google/Apple/Meta branding, no watermarks, no hands, no fingers, no script or comic fonts

recommended_generators.nano_banana_pro_gemini_3_pro_image: Best for OG card and any slot needing in-image text rendering — SOTA typography fidelity.
recommended_generators.nano_banana_gemini_2_5_flash_image: Fast iteration, edits, style transfer; weaker text — use for the LinkedIn banner and GitHub hero where there's no text.
recommended_generators.imagen_4: Strong photorealism if you want a photographic banner direction.
recommended_generators.midjourney_v7: Best aesthetic ceiling for editorial/illustrative variants. Use --ar flags (--ar 4:1 for banners, --ar 1.91:1 for OG, --ar 16:9 for general).
recommended_generators.flux_pro_1_1_or_dalle_3: Solid fallbacks; treat them as second-pass options.

images.use_case: LinkedIn profile banner for an Android Developer specializing in Kotlin and KMP/CMP.
images.safe_zone_note: LinkedIn crops the bottom-left ~280x280 area behind the profile photo. Keep that region clean — no critical text or focal subject in the left ~20% of the frame.

variants.label: Original — geometric multi-device silhouettes
variants.style: Clean, minimal, geometric. Subtle gradient backdrop. Tech-leaning but not cliché — no binary rain, no glowing circuits, no robot hands.
variants.subject: Abstract composition suggesting cross-platform mobile development: a soft cluster of overlapping device-shape silhouettes (phone + tablet + watch + desktop monitor) rendered as outlined geometric forms in light strokes, off-center to the right side of the banner. Empty negative space on the left where the LinkedIn profile photo sits.
color_palette: subtle gradient from navy to deep navy
variants.in_image_text: none — text is added by LinkedIn (name, headline). Keep the banner pure visual.
variants.negative_prompt: no text, no logos, no faces, no people, no binary code, no glowing circuits, no neon, no AI-generated person stereotypes, no Anthropic/Google/Apple branding, no stock-photo skylines
variants.full_prompt: A 4:1 horizontal LinkedIn banner (1584x396), minimal geometric composition. On the right two-thirds of the frame, a soft cluster of four overlapping device silhouettes (a phone, a tablet, a smartwatch, and a desktop monitor) rendered as thin outlined geometric forms in Cobalt Navy (#004AAD) on a subtly graduated background that fades from #004AAD top-right to a deeper navy bottom-right. The left third of the frame is intentionally empty negative space (the LinkedIn profile photo overlays this region). Lighting: flat, ambient, no harsh shadows — Swiss/International Typographic Style aesthetic. Mood: calm, professional, signal-over-noise. Crisp vector-clean edges, light stroke weight (~2px equivalent). No text, no logos, no faces, no glowing circuits, no neon, no stock-photo skylines.

variants.label: Editorial macro photography — builder's desk
variants.style: Photographic. Editorial product-photography feel, shallow depth of field, real materials — closer to a thoughtful Monocle / It's Nice That spread than a tech-stock photo.
variants.subject: A horizontal macro photograph of a builder's desk surface shot from a low 30-degree angle: the right side of the frame holds a closed matte-black notebook with an unbranded pen resting on it, a brass ruler at a slight diagonal, and the corner of a smartphone partially visible — all on a textured off-white paper or linen surface. The left third of the frame is gently out-of-focus negative space with soft warm bokeh, leaving room for the LinkedIn profile photo overlay.
color_palette: single accent of #004AAD on a small object detail
variants.negative_prompt: no laptops, no glowing screens, no people, no hands, no faces, no headphones, no coffee cliché steam, no stock-photo cleanliness, no Apple/Google logos
variants.full_prompt: A 4:1 horizontal LinkedIn banner photograph (1584x396), shot with an 85mm macro lens at f/2.0 producing shallow depth of field and soft warm bokeh. A builder's desk surface seen from a low 30-degree angle: on the right two-thirds, a closed matte-black hardcover notebook with an unbranded pen resting on it, a brass ruler at a 15-degree diagonal, and the corner of a phone partially visible at the edge — all on a textured linen-weave off-white surface. One small object carries a single Cobalt Navy (#004AAD) accent (a bookmark ribbon or pen detail). The left third of the frame is intentionally empty, soft-focus, slightly warmer in tone, reserved for the LinkedIn profile photo overlay. Lighting: soft window light from the upper-left, golden-hour warmth, no harsh highlights. Mood: editorial, craft-oriented, considered. Subtle film grain. No people, no hands, no laptops, no glowing screens, no coffee steam, no logos.

variants.label: Isometric 3D — KMP platform stack
variants.style: Isometric 3D render. Flat-shaded, low-poly, restrained palette — closer to a clean architecture diagram than a marketing render. References: dribbble isometric illustrations, Figma's branding aesthetic.
variants.subject: Four floating, slightly offset rectangular platform-tiles arranged in an ascending isometric stack on the right two-thirds of the frame. From bottom to top, each tile is a stylised abstraction of: an Android phone, a desktop window, a smartwatch face, and a tablet. Tiles are connected by thin vertical lines suggesting a shared codebase running through them. Pure white background on the left side for the profile photo overlay.
color_palette: #7F52FF single Kotlin-purple accent on the top tile
variants.negative_prompt: no realistic device renders, no Android mascot, no Kotlin logo, no glowing edges, no shadows that imply photorealism, no people, no text
variants.full_prompt: A 4:1 horizontal LinkedIn banner (1584x396), pure isometric 3D illustration on a flat white #FFFFFF background. Four flat-shaded low-poly platform tiles floating at 30-degree isometric angle, ascending diagonally up and to the right across the right two-thirds of the frame. Bottom tile: stylised Android phone outline. Second: desktop window. Third: round smartwatch. Top: tablet. Each tile is filled in Cobalt Navy (#004AAD), edged in #0A0A0A, with thin #0A0A0A vertical lines connecting them suggesting a shared codebase. The top tile carries a small Kotlin-purple (#7F52FF) accent dot. The left third of the frame is intentionally empty white space for the LinkedIn profile photo overlay. Mood: structural, deliberate, architecture-diagram cleanliness. Crisp vector edges, no gradients, no glow, no shadows. No realistic device renders, no logos, no people, no text.

variants.label: Typographic — fading Kotlin code fragment
variants.style: Pure typographic composition, Swiss/International Typographic Style, monospace as visual texture. References: Kvell, Pentagram editorial layouts, GitHub octicons restraint.
variants.subject: A horizontal composition of monospace text: a single Kotlin code line — 'fun build(): Future = compose(android, ios, desktop, web)' — set in IBM Plex Mono, ranged left, occupying the right two-thirds of the frame. The code fades from full-opacity Cobalt Navy on the right to barely visible toward the centre, never reaching the left third. The left third is empty white for the profile photo overlay.
variants.in_image_text: Yes — exact string in double quotes: "fun build(): Future = compose(android, ios, desktop, web)". Render in IBM Plex Mono (or any clean monospace fallback).
variants.negative_prompt: no syntax-highlighted IDE colours beyond the navy, no terminal frame, no window chrome, no faces, no decorative borders, no comic fonts
variants.full_prompt: A 4:1 horizontal LinkedIn banner (1584x396) on a pure white #FFFFFF background. A single line of monospace code rendered in IBM Plex Mono, exact text: "fun build(): Future = compose(android, ios, desktop, web)". The text spans the right two-thirds of the frame, fading from 100% opacity Cobalt Navy (#004AAD) on the right to ~5% opacity near the centre, completely transparent on the left third (which is reserved for the LinkedIn profile photo overlay). A thin #0A0A0A horizontal rule sits 12px below the code baseline, only as wide as the visible portion of text. No window chrome, no terminal frame, no syntax highlighting beyond the single navy colour. Mood: Swiss typographic, code-as-poetry, quietly confident. No decorative elements, no faces, no people, no logos.

images.use_case: Optional hero image at the top of the IronManYG/IronManYG profile README. Same visual family as the LinkedIn banner so the two profiles feel like one brand.
images.safe_zone_note: GitHub renders this at full width on desktop and scaled-down on mobile. Don't put critical detail in the outer 5% — it can clip on narrow viewports.

variants.label: Original — dual-stroke waveform / signal
variants.style: Slightly more playful than LinkedIn — this surface tolerates more personality.
variants.subject: A horizontal composition: stylized waveform or signal pattern flowing left to right, rendered in two stroke widths (thin Cobalt Navy + thicker pure-black). Could be read as audio (EchoJournal nod) or as code rhythm. Off-center; leaves breathing room on both ends.
variants.negative_prompt: no text, no logos, no faces, no people, no binary code, no glowing circuits, no neon, no Anthropic/Google/Apple branding, no stock-photo skylines
variants.full_prompt: A 4:1 horizontal GitHub README hero image (1280x320) on a pure white #FFFFFF background. A horizontal waveform composition flowing left to right across the centre of the frame: two parallel signal lines, one thin (~1.5px) in Cobalt Navy (#004AAD) and one thicker (~3px) in #0A0A0A, oscillating in irregular but harmonic peaks. The waveform fades in from 30% opacity at the left edge, reaches full intensity at the centre-right, and tapers off softly past the right third. Generous breathing room above and below. Mood: active, builder, signal-over-noise — could be read as audio waveform or code rhythm. Crisp vector edges. No text, no logos, no faces, no neon, no glow, no grid background.

variants.label: Topographic contour map — abstract terrain
variants.style: Editorial cartographic — references USGS topo lines, Field Notes covers, Kinfolk magazine restraint. Layered linework over flat background.
variants.subject: Concentric topographic contour lines forming an abstract elevation map, off-centred to the right two-thirds of the frame. Lines are progressively darker as they move toward the centre of the contour cluster, suggesting elevation (or focus). Left third of the frame is sparse, with one or two thin outermost rings drifting off the edge.
color_palette: #004AAD contour lines varying in opacity from 15% to 100%
variants.negative_prompt: no labels, no compass roses, no map markers, no terrain shading, no realism, no faces, no text
variants.full_prompt: A 4:1 horizontal GitHub README hero image (1280x320) on a pure white #FFFFFF background. An abstract topographic-style contour-line composition: ~12 concentric irregular closed curves nested inside each other, off-centred toward the right two-thirds of the frame. Lines are drawn in Cobalt Navy (#004AAD) at progressively higher opacity moving inward — outermost ring at 15% opacity, innermost ring rendered in #0A0A0A. Stroke weight ~1.5px throughout. The outermost two rings drift off the right edge of the frame. The left third holds only one or two faint outermost arcs and otherwise generous white space. Mood: editorial, layered, considered, exploratory. Vector-crisp edges, no shading, no fill, no gradients. No labels, no map markers, no compass, no text, no faces, no logos.

variants.label: Constellation grid — connected projects
variants.style: Information-graphic minimalism, references: Stripe Press book covers, Edward Tufte plates. Dot-and-line network on a light grid.
variants.subject: A constellation-style network of small filled dots (representing shipped projects) connected by thin straight lines, distributed across the right two-thirds of the frame. Six larger dots act as anchor nodes (the six pinned projects), with several smaller satellite dots branching off each. Lines are sparse, not a dense graph. A faint dotted baseline grid sits underneath at very low opacity.
variants.negative_prompt: no text labels on nodes, no arrows, no force-directed mess, no constellation names, no zodiac, no faces
variants.full_prompt: A 4:1 horizontal GitHub README hero image (1280x320) on a pure white #FFFFFF background. A faint dotted baseline grid at 5% opacity covers the full frame. On top of it, an abstract constellation-style network: six larger filled dots (~6px diameter) in #0A0A0A act as anchor nodes, distributed asymmetrically across the right two-thirds of the frame. Each anchor has 2-4 smaller satellite dots (~3px) in Cobalt Navy (#004AAD) branching off it, connected by thin (~1px) Cobalt Navy lines. The graph is intentionally sparse — generous white space between clusters, no overlapping lines. Left third holds only one small Cobalt Navy satellite dot drifting on its own. Mood: shipped, connected, network-of-projects, lived-in. Vector-clean. No text labels, no arrows, no constellation names, no faces, no logos.

variants.label: Typographic — terminal prompt line
variants.style: Pure typographic composition, terminal/monospace aesthetic without any window chrome.
variants.subject: A single horizontal line of monospace text reading '> hussain.gaddal --kotlin --multiplatform' followed by a solid block cursor, set ranged-left. A thin Cobalt Navy underline sits below the entire text. Generous white space above and below.
variants.in_image_text: Yes — exact string in double quotes: "> hussain.gaddal --kotlin --multiplatform" plus a trailing solid block █ cursor. Render in IBM Plex Mono.
variants.negative_prompt: no terminal window chrome, no traffic-light buttons, no syntax-highlight greens or yellows, no scanlines, no glow, no text other than the specified string
variants.full_prompt: A 4:1 horizontal GitHub README hero image (1280x320) on a pure white #FFFFFF background. A single line of IBM Plex Mono text, vertically centred, ranged-left starting at ~8% from the left edge. Exact text: the chevron ">" rendered in Cobalt Navy (#004AAD), followed by " hussain.gaddal --kotlin --multiplatform" rendered in #0A0A0A, followed by a solid block █ cursor in #0A0A0A. Below the entire text, a thin (~1.5px) Cobalt Navy (#004AAD) horizontal underline running from the chevron to just past the cursor. Generous breathing room above and below. No terminal window chrome, no traffic-light buttons, no scanlines, no glow, no syntax-highlight colours beyond what's specified. Mood: builder, dev-native, approachable, no-frills. No other text, no faces, no logos.
